title: Design: long and special customer names in rows and the Customer filter
refs: SV-11718 (Reports Story 2 S2-R2 Reports Story 3 S3-R4 Reports Story 1 S1-R6)
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Reports — Page Access', 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts' and 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new category for this test, category A, priced by a new matrix for this test, matrix A, with one cost range ($0.00 and up) whose Default rule is Markup % 35.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 10.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, with a long name with spaces of exactly 50 characters (for example Northern Alberta Heavy Equipment Fleet Pricing Tier).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, with a long name with no spaces of exactly 50 characters (for example NorthernAlbertaHeavyEquipmentFleetPricingTierPlanX).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer C, with a name with the characters & " ' < > in it (for example A&B "Fleet" O'Neil <Tier>).
  • Make sure customers A, B and C are on tier A for work orders, each with an invoiced work order today with a part in category A.
  • Use a desktop browser window exactly 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so the screen matches the design pictures' size.
custom_steps:
1. Open Reports › Sales by Tier.
  2. Pick customers A, B and C in the Customer filter.
  3. Open tier A's row.
  4. Open the Customer filter.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Sales by Tier opens.

Step 2:

  • Tier A's row shows.

Step 3:

  • Customer A's and customer B's long names each stay inside their own row, wrapped or shortened with "...".
  • Customer C's name shows character for character, & " ' < > included.
  • Every column stays visible and the page does not scroll sideways.

Step 4:

  • Each long name wraps or is shortened with "..." inside the list.
  • No name runs past the list's edge.
